explain.say: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, reaching around 100 kilometres per hour in short sprints. Its whole body is built for acceleration and speed, at the cost of strength and stamina.

explain.say: Its very flexible spine coils and uncoils like a spring with every stride. At full speed a stride is about 7 metres long, with the cheetah taking around three strides a second.

explain.say: But speed costs energy and makes heat. Most chases cover only a few hundred metres and are over in well under a minute, then the cheetah must rest, panting, before it can even eat.

faq.q: How fast can a cheetah run?
faq.a: Cheetahs have been timed at about 29 metres per second, around 100 kilometres per hour, in short bursts. Just as important, they can speed up, slow down and turn very sharply, which is what catches prey.
asks: What is the top speed of a cheetah?
Is the cheetah the fastest animal?

faq.q: How does a cheetah's spine help it run?
faq.a: The spine bends deeply as the legs gather under the body, then straightens as they stretch out. This lengthens each stride and works like a spring, adding speed.
asks: Why is a cheetah's back so bendy?
What does the spine do when a cheetah runs?

faq.a: Most cats pull their claws right in to keep them sharp. A cheetah's claws stay partly out, gripping the ground like running spikes, and a large dewclaw helps it hook prey.
asks: Why do cheetah claws stick out?

faq.q: Why can't cheetahs run for long?
faq.a: Sprinting burns energy very fast and builds up heat. Cheetahs usually chase for only a few hundred metres and then must rest to recover.
asks: How long can a cheetah sprint?
Why do cheetahs get tired so quickly?

faq.q: Why is a cheetah faster than a lion?
faq.a: Cheetahs are slim and light, about 20 to 70 kilograms, with long legs and a flexible spine. Lions are much heavier and built for strength to wrestle big prey, so they stalk close and finish with a short rush.
asks: Why are lions slower than cheetahs?
